appraisal_events.evidence: "c'était bien avec elle, devenue une actrice célèbre... que la duchesse de Guermantes causait"; "c'était Rachel qui, en réalité, recevait chez la princesse"; society deserts the Berma's tea to hear Rachel recite.
appraisal_events.explanation: Rachel, once dismissed by the Berma as a lowly 'grue,' is now shown as a celebrated actress who commands the duchesse de Guermantes's intimacy and draws all of fashionable Paris to her recital, effectively becoming the true hostess of the Guermantes gathering.

appraisal_events.evidence: "les heures passaient et personne n'arrivait chez la Berma"; "il y avait vide absolu et mort"; the gathering is described as "un repas funéraire" with "gâteaux funéraires."
appraisal_events.explanation: The Berma is abandoned by nearly all her invited guests, who prefer Rachel's fashionable recital at the Guermantes party; her tea collapses into a funereal, deserted scene that the narrator frames with sustained, sympathetic pathos.

status_effects.explanation: Rachel's local standing rises sharply: the once-scorned actress now draws society's attention and enjoys the duchesse de Guermantes's chosen friendship, eclipsing the Berma as the center of the fashionable world's interest.
The Berma's local standing collapses in this passage as the social world she once could command deserts her entirely for Rachel's more fashionable event.
Nearly everyone invited fails to appear, leaving the Berma's gathering literally emptied out ('vide absolu et mort') while the valued social space has moved elsewhere.

ambiguities: Rachel's ascent is narrated with an undercurrent of irony about society's fickle preference for fashion over the Berma's genuine artistic greatness (the Berma's own bitter remark, 'Une Rachel donnant une fête chez la princesse de Guermantes...'), which qualifies but does not negate the plainly narrated fact of her elevated local standing in this passage.

The passage explicitly leaves undecided what the duchesse de Guermantes's new intimacy with Rachel means for the duchesse's own reputation (evidence of her having been unfairly judged snobbish before, versus evidence of a mediocre, restless intelligence), so no status effect is assigned to the duchesse on this point.
